_meta.description: Medical jargon to plain-English mapping. Each entry maps a medical term (lowercase) to a plain-language alternative and a category. Sources: MedlinePlus Consumer Health Vocabulary, NHS Plain English guidance, CDC Clear Communication Index.

abscess.plain: a pocket of pus caused by infection

angina.plain: chest pain caused by reduced blood flow to the heart

biopsy.plain: removing a small piece of tissue to test for disease

bronchitis.plain: swelling of the airways in the lungs

cardiovascular.plain: related to the heart and blood vessels

catheter.plain: a thin tube inserted into the body

cerebrovascular.plain: related to blood vessels in the brain

comorbidity.plain: having more than one health condition at the same time

contraindicated.plain: should not be used because it may be harmful

coronary.plain: related to the arteries that supply blood to the heart

creatinine.plain: a waste product measured to check kidney function

cyanosis.plain: bluish colour of the skin from lack of oxygen

deep vein thrombosis.plain: blood clot in a deep vein, usually in the leg

diabetes mellitus.plain: a condition where blood sugar levels are too high

diagnosis.plain: identifying what illness or condition someone has

dialysis.plain: treatment that filters your blood when your kidneys cannot

diastolic.plain: the bottom number in a blood pressure reading

distal.plain: farther from the centre of the body

diuretic.plain: medicine that helps your body get rid of extra water

dosage.plain: the amount of medicine to take

electrocardiogram.plain: a test that records the electrical activity of the heart (ECG)

embolism.plain: a blockage in a blood vessel, usually by a blood clot

endemic.plain: regularly found in a certain area or population

endoscopy.plain: using a thin camera tube to look inside the body

epidemiology.plain: the study of how diseases spread in populations

exacerbation.plain: a flare-up or worsening of symptoms

gastroenteritis.plain: stomach bug (inflammation of the stomach and intestines)

gastrointestinal.plain: related to the stomach and intestines

haematoma.plain: a solid swelling of clotted blood under the skin

haemoglobin.plain: the protein in red blood cells that carries oxygen

hypoxia.plain: not enough oxygen reaching the body's tissues

immunosuppressant.plain: medicine that lowers the body's immune response

in vitro.plain: done in a laboratory (outside the body)

infarction.plain: death of tissue due to blocked blood supply

inflammation.plain: redness, swelling, and pain — the body's response to injury or infection

intravenous.plain: into a vein (usually through a drip)

ischaemia.plain: reduced blood flow to part of the body

laceration.plain: a deep cut or tear in the skin

lesion.plain: an area of damaged or abnormal tissue

magnetic resonance imaging.plain: MRI scan (uses magnets to create detailed images)

metastasis.plain: cancer spreading from where it started to other parts of the body

morbidity.plain: the state of being ill or the rate of illness

mortality.plain: death or the rate of death

nephrology.plain: the study and treatment of kidney diseases

neurology.plain: the study and treatment of brain and nerve conditions

neuropathy.plain: nerve damage, often causing numbness or pain

nil by mouth.plain: do not eat or drink anything

non-invasive.plain: does not involve cutting into the body

obesity.plain: being very overweight in a way that is harmful to health

palliative.plain: treatment focused on comfort rather than cure

pathology.plain: the study of disease, or the lab that tests tissue samples

peripheral.plain: in the outer parts of the body (arms, legs)

platelet.plain: a tiny blood cell that helps blood clot

pneumonia.plain: infection that inflames the air sacs in the lungs

prognosis.plain: the likely course or outcome of a disease

proximal.plain: closer to the centre of the body

resection.plain: surgical removal of part of an organ or tissue

systolic.plain: the top number in a blood pressure reading

thrombosis.plain: a blood clot inside a blood vessel

transient ischaemic attack.plain: mini-stroke (temporary blockage of blood to the brain)

ultrasound.plain: a scan using sound waves to create images of inside the body

ventilator.plain: a machine that helps you breathe
